title: Showcase: two aircraft, proven
summary: Fly the scratch quad and the SDK drone for the family, and show the mass budget, thrust-to-weight and drift numbers behind both of them.
materials: the scratch quad from weeks 1 and 2
the programmable SDK drone from week 3
the mass budget and thrust-to-weight numbers from season 3 week 7
tri-fold science fair board or a large sheet of card
the Maker's Log, open to weeks 1 through 3

steps.title: Plan the presentation
steps.body:
Write four numbers on the board: the scratch quad's mass budget and thrust-to-weight ratio from season 3 week 7. Also write the smallest and largest drift distances from week 3's square flights.

Plan the presentation in this order.

1. Show the scratch quad and explain what thrust-to-weight means, using its own measured number.

2. Fly the scratch quad in a short free hover.

3. Show the SDK drone and fly its coded square, live.

4. Show the board's drift numbers and say how far the square drifted from a perfect square.

Be ready for one question about which aircraft was harder to build and why.

figure.alt: A simple top-down room layout for the showcase: a presentation board on the left holding the mass, thrust-to-weight and drift numbers, a marked hover zone in the middle for the scratch quad, a dashed taped square on the right for the SDK drone's coded flight, and the family's viewing area along the bottom facing all three.

steps.title: Rehearse both flights
steps.body:
Fly the scratch quad's hover once at demo settings. Fly the SDK drone's coded square once on the same taped square used for the real numbers.

Practise explaining thrust-to-weight in one sentence a family member with no background in it could repeat back correctly.
checklist: The mass budget and thrust-to-weight numbers are ready to state clearly
The scratch quad hovers reliably at demo settings
The SDK drone's coded square flies on the same taped square used for the real numbers
I can answer one question comparing the two aircraft honestly

steps.title: Show the family
steps.body:
Gather the family and present in the order rehearsed: the scratch quad's numbers and hover, then the SDK drone's coded square and its drift result.

Invite one question and answer it honestly, naming anything that surprised you about either aircraft.

steps.title: Show it
steps.prompt: A short recording of both flights in front of the family, plus a photo of the board with all four numbers
